best_for: People who want to chat with AI models on their own Windows, Mac or Linux computer, offline and without paying per message, and who have the memory to hold a model.
description:
GPT4All is a desktop chat app from Nomic AI that downloads open large language models and runs them on your own computer, using the llama.cpp engine. Nomic says no data leaves your machine when you chat with a local model.

You find models through a built-in browser that searches Hugging Face for GGUF files, download one, and talk to it in a chat window, switching models as you go. LocalDocs lets you point the app at a folder so answers can draw on your own files, and each reply shows which files it used. A Python SDK gives your own scripts the same models.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: GPT4All costs nothing and is released under the MIT license. Local models need no API key and no GPU. You can also add remote models from providers such as OpenAI, Groq or Mistral with your own key, and those chats go to that provider.

points.title: Memory matters most
points.text: Nomic lists 16 GB of RAM as the minimum, or 8 GB for small 3-billion-parameter models, and the processor must support AVX or AVX2. For speed it recommends a graphics card with 8 GB or more on a PC, or an M2 Pro Mac. The app is tuned for models of 3 to 13 billion parameters.

points.title: Oldest supported systems
points.text: Nomic lists Windows 10, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and macOS Monterey 12.6 as the minimums. The Mac app is one universal build and works best on Apple silicon. Nomic's own Linux build is x64 only.

points.title: Windows installer and silent setup
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 10 versions, all x64; only 3.8.0 also has an Arm64 build. The installer removes the previous version first, and runs unattended with `install --accept-licenses --confirm-command --accept-messages`.

points.title: Linux comes from a community Flatpak
points.text: The Flathub package, for x64 and Arm64, is maintained by the community rather than by Nomic, and Flathub does not mark it as verified. macOS and Linux list only the current version.

points.title: A local API for other apps
points.text: Turn on the local API server in the settings and other programs can use your models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on port 4891. It listens only on localhost, over plain HTTP, and can add LocalDocs snippets to its answers.

points.title: No new release since February 2025
points.text: Version 3.10.0, released in February 2025, is the newest version on every platform in this listing.
